multi_speaker_pages_split: Trustpilot pages 1 and 2 (www.etsy.com and www.etsy.com?page=2) contained multiple buyer reviews. Each distinct buyer was split into a separate finding per the multi-speaker rule. Same treatment applied to Sitejabber (etsy.com) and ConsumerAffairs (etsy.com). Identical URLs appear across multiple findings; each references a different buyer voice.
2_truncated_sources: Four Trustpilot reviews (gamesforu F-X14, Steven Olive, Doone Watts F-X15, Robin) had review text truncated by Trustpilot's page display (reviews end mid-sentence with "..."). These were degraded to Part 4 because the incomplete verbatim does not fully support the behavior description. The page itself was directly fetched; the truncation is a display limitation of the source platform, not an access issue.
findings_forced_to_provisional: ConsumerAffairs findings (F-P07, F-P08, F-P09) were planned as direct_verified but ConsumerAffairs returned a 403 error on verification fetch. Verbatim text was captured from search engine index/snippet. Reclassified as blocked_url_index_verified. SimilarWeb and Semrush findings (F-P01 through F-P06) were captured from search snippets as source pages could not be directly fetched. Capital One Shopping (F-P13, F-P17), ElectroIQ (F-P12), Yaguara (F-P14), Whop (F-P15), and Willow Commerce (F-P16) degraded to provisional due to uncertainty about whether pages were directly fetched by automated research tools; all contain extensive verbatim text but fetch confirmation could not be independently verified. Marketplace Pulse (F-P18) degraded for same reason.
4_source_type_ambiguities: ConsumerAffairs buyer reviews classified as buyer_review applying same logic as Trustpilot/Sitejabber per protocol (speaker is clearly a buyer of an Etsy purchase reviewing that experience). Motley Fool earnings call transcripts (F-18, F-19) classified as article (publication hosting transcript). Marketplace Pulse data tracking page (F-P18) classified as report. Capital One Shopping statistical compilations (F-P13, F-P17) classified as report (aggregated data from SEC filings and analytics platforms).
5_coverage_gaps__reddit: Reddit (r/Etsy, r/BuyItForLife) was entirely inaccessible due to web_fetch tool blocking and absence from web search engine index results. Reddit URLs provided in the task brief (https://www.reddit.com/r/Etsy/, https://www.reddit.com/r/BuyItForLife/search/?q=etsy) could not be fetched. Fourteen distinct search query variants targeting Reddit content returned zero Reddit URLs. This represents a significant gap in direct buyer community voice data.
6_coverage_gaps__tiktok: TikTok #etsyhaul content identified but could not be fetched or transcribed. Buyer discovery behavior via TikTok is referenced indirectly in other findings but no direct buyer voice from TikTok was captured.
7_container_ambiguity: Trustpilot hosts separate review profiles for www.etsy.com and etsy.co.uk. Findings from the www.etsy.com profile (pages 1 and 2) are confirmed fetched and classified as direct_verified. Findings from the etsy.co.uk profile (F-P10, F-P11) were not confirmed fetched from a separate access and are classified as blocked_url_index_verified.
8_time_window_exclusions: Three Sitejabber reviews (Richard M Feb 2025, C.W. Dec 2024, zeroryu J Dec 2024) were excluded from Parts 1–2 as outside the April 2025–April 2026 time window. The eRank 2024 buyer survey (late 2024 publication) was similarly excluded. These are documented in Part 4.
9_decomposition_completeness: SD-03 and SD-04 (Reddit sub-searches) returned zero usable results due to tool access limitations, not absence of content. SD-12 (buyer survey data from 2025–2026) found no survey published within the time window; the most recent identified was eRank's late-2024 survey (outside window). All other sub-searches returned at least partial results.
10_clean_count: Part 1 contains 20 clean findings (11 buyer review, 9 aggregated data), at the upper bound of the 10–20 expected range. This reflects successful direct access to Trustpilot (2 pages), Sitejabber (1 page), Etsy Investor Relations press releases (4 quarters), and multiple trade publication articles. No verification bar was lowered to achieve this count.
11_seller_voice_exclusion: Two blog sources were identified containing buyer behavior observations reported by sellers (Hunting for Vintage blog commenter, Sketchy Notions blog author). Both were excluded as D2 territory per protocol. The ConsumerAffairs review set and Sitejabber review set both contained some ambiguous seller-vs-buyer voices; only reviews with clear buyer identification were included.
